scope: Independent read-only Mach-O/fileset, byte, chained-fixup and declared-KPI comparison. No source edits, builds, SSH, hardware or runtime test.

correction_to_preliminary_report.finding: The preliminary old-kext __TEXT and 15 __DATA_CONST deltas were parser artifacts, not changed linked bytes. Preserve that report; this review supersedes only those comparisons.
correction_to_preliminary_report.cause: MH_KEXT_BUNDLE fileoffs, section offsets and symtab offsets are relative to each fileset member header; slicing them as collection-absolute reads unrelated bytes. The kernel member uses absolute offsets.
correction_to_preliminary_report.independent_crosscheck: For every file-backed kext segment, entry_header_fileoff + segment.fileoff equals outer.__PRELINK_TEXT.fileoff + segment.vmaddr - outer.__PRELINK_TEXT.vmaddr in both collections.

interpretation: One new 80-byte LC_FILESET_ENTRY is inserted in both outer and embedded-kernel command lists; ncmds and sizeofcmds increase, moving LC_DYLD_CHAINED_FIXUPS within each header.

Outer PRELINK_TEXT grows by 0x1c000 for the new observer. Existing kernel/kext VM addresses stay fixed. PRELINK_INFO moves upward by 0x1c000 and grows in content by 1908 bytes; its allocated 0x24000 span stays fixed.

The broad kernel/outer LINKEDIT filesize and vmsize grow by 0x1c038 because this aggregate tail includes appended kext, relocated PRELINK_INFO, alignment and chained-fixup payload; this is not a mutation of retained kernel symbols or old kext linkedit.
Both __PRELINK_INFO section descriptors and segment descriptors track the relocated/new-sized metadata.

data_pointer_fixups.encoding: DYLD_CHAINED_PTR_64_KERNEL_CACHE; target = outer __TEXT.vmaddr + low30; next is 4-byte stride; parsed from actual chain starts, including packed kmod 4-byte-aligned pointers.

nonchain_section_changes.only: packed kmod_info.address and kmod_info.size, synthesized by kc-tools/lib/linker.c:881-905

named_dyld_bind_stream_independent_check.method: Decoded original standalone LC_DYLD_INFO_ONLY regular/lazy bind opcodes, including signed addends and uint64 offset arithmetic; independently decoded each linked slot through the actual kernel-cache chain target.

only_special_case.explanation: kc-tools lib/linker.c:1537,1553,1647-1655 deliberately maps unresolved dyld_stub_binder to the panic trampoline. It is not an undeclared callable KPI or newly required userspace resolver. All normal kernel imports bind to their named target.

imports.baseline_norm: dyld_stub_binder appears undefined in all 49 retained standalone/member symbol tables. In this observer its GOT slot is intentionally bound to the kernel _panic trampoline by kc-tools, as independently verified from original bind opcodes and linked bytes.

limits: This admits artifact binding only. No complete packet, host opt-in, collector/supervisor binding, hardware MMIO safety under the actual boot, or runtime observation is admitted.

The earlier source review proves shared PHY/PMGR writer translation units absent from this observer build. It does not make the whole boot PCIe-write-free: retained m1n1 HV initialization calls pcie_shutdown(). NO P_PCIE_INIT remains the superseding plan.
GPU observer remains on hold. Retained unrelated baseline kexts are preserved, not newly qualified by this review.

method.parsing: Original read-only Python Mach-O/fileset parser; embedded MH_KEXT_BUNDLE uses entry-relative offsets, kernel uses absolute offsets; reject symbol STAB entries before undefined/defined classification.
method.chained_pointer_source: Pinned XNU EXTERNAL_HEADERS/mach-o/fixup-chains.h:200-211; format8 parsed through starts_in_image/segment/page chains rather than assuming 8-byte section alignment.
